    Strategy game · 2026 · in development

    Houses of Fading Suns

    A turn-based hex strategy game in the spirit of Emperor of the Fading Suns, built in Godot. Noble houses fight over several planets, each one its own hex map, and over the space between them.

    • Godot 4.7
    • 699 commits since 7 Sep 2026
    • Windows build
    Source on GitHub →

    How it plays

    Space

    Any ship can launch to orbit for 1 Fuel and jump from orbit to orbit. Ships burn no Fuel while in space, and crews aboard don't need upkeep. Cargo pods carry resources down to the planets.

    Economy

    Roads carry what mines, farms and wells produce to a Stockpile. Three Agoras on every planet buy and sell Food, Energy, Metals and rarer goods, and refill a tenth of their stock each turn.

    Research and demons

    Universities and Labs research structure and unit techs from books. Books in a Monastery are safe. Books kept in a Lab or out in the field can draw demons.

    Combat

    Each attack rolls to see whether it damages the target; a hit deals 1 damage. Weapons are rated against hard, soft and air targets. Area strikes wound every unit in the enemy stack, and ranged units fire across several hexes.

    Wrecks and capture

    Units aren't destroyed outright: they are wrecked and can be repaired back into service. Infantry can rout and escape combat, and can capture enemy vehicles. Vehicles burn Energy and are abandoned when they run dry.

    Resources

    Food, Energy, Metals, Fuel, Trace, Exotics, Chemicals, Biochems, Electronics, Wetware and Ceramsteel.

    Tabletop RPG rules · 2026 · draft

    RUST

    A rules-light dark fantasy RPG in the vein of Mörk Borg. Every test is a pool of six-sided dice in four colours: you need one success to pass, and the dark dice take successes away.

    • d6 dice pools
    • Strength · Agility · Mind
    • 12-page draft

    Roll a test

    4
    1
    2
    2

    The rulebook's own example: a twice-wounded scholar with 3 Mind and a Rune Atlas reads old runes on a wall, in the dark and in a hurry. One success gets through, and the misfortune draws a monster's attention.

    success misfortune: −1 success, complication vanquish: −1 success, death on a failed defense

    The four dice

    DieComes fromRollsEffect
    BaseAttribute, advantages, good gear5–6Success
    SkillOne relevant skill, outside combat4–6Success
    StressPenalties, darkness, haste, trauma6Misfortune: removes a success and adds a complication
    WoundEach wound the character carries6Vanquish: removes a success; on a failed defense roll, death

    Making a character

    Attributes

    Strength (power, endurance), Agility (speed, precision) and Mind (intelligence, perception, willpower). Pick one set and place it: balanced 4/3/3, drop-stat 4/4/2 or min-max 5/3/2.

    A starved prisoner who survived years of torture takes 5/3/2 as Strength 2, Agility 3, Mind 5.

    Skills and abilities

    Pick three skills, such as Lockpicking, Herbalism, Monster Knowledge or Intimidation. Abilities are unique powers with their own rules: Looting, Treasure Hunting, Good Sleep (at least 3 Stamina on rest), Making Fire, Animal Taming.

    Stamina and Luck

    Stamina starts at 1d6 and pays for dodging, extra effort and minor harm. At 0 you are Tired; below 0, unconscious. Luck starts at 1: spend it to reroll or to cheat death, and earn more by playing your failures dramatically.

    Fear and trauma

    Failed Mind saves bring fear, from Pale and Nervous up to Panic and Fainting. A failed save with a misfortune leaves a trauma, like a phobia or an addiction, and each trauma adds a permanent stress die.

    From the bestiary

    Swarm of rats

    Wounds – · Morale PC×3 · Bites

    Surrounds every character at once. You can't evade, only swing wide and tear rats off yourself. They keep away from an open torch.

    Bandit

    Wounds 2 · Morale PC×2 · Club and knife

    Always outnumbers the party two to one. Wants your valuables, not your life, and runs as soon as you show you can fight back.

    Troll

    Wounds 4 · Morale 3 · Tree trunk · BIG

    Three metres tall and slow-witted. Heals a wound at the start of every round, and a wide swing can knock down everyone in front of it.

    Board game variant · 2026

    Nevsky: Swantopolk II

    A variant for Nevsky: Teutons and Rus in Collision. It adds new lords, random initiative, river rowing and hungry armies that eat their horses, with every component ready to print.

    Download all files to print →

    • 10 new lord mats
    • Art of War cards R1–R21, T2–T21
    • Print at 100% on A4

    What changes

    New lords

    Tverdilo Ivankovich is a Rus lord allied with the Teutons: his Seat is Pskov, so the Teutons must conquer Pskov to muster him. Pelgusiy is a new Rus lord seated at Neva. Aleksandr and Andrey lose their Seat in Novgorod and start in Rusa.

    Random initiative

    Plan one Command card more than the season allows, shuffle the stack and take away the bottom card unseen. Nobody knows which lord moves next.

    Rowing

    A new command for Summer and Rasputitsa: one action moves a group any distance along connected waterways, past strongholds and enemy lords. It needs a Boat per Provender and two per Horse or Loot.

    Pocket Coins

    Lords keep their own Coin. In Levy it stands in for Lordship; in Campaign it buys a cart, sled, boat or ship on the spot, even in foreign land.

    Simpler battles

    Up to three lords a side, no positions, no flanking. The defender allocates hits freely, and pursuit is fought only by horse.

    Winter cavalry

    In Early and Late Winter, a group with more Horse than Foot gets +1 Command for its leading lord.

    Combat, step by step

    When both sides act in the same step, the defender goes first.

    1. Combat manoeuvres from event cards
    2. Ambush: Peshy Voi strike before archery outside strongholds
    3. River Assault: Ushkuyniki with a boat strike first along a waterway
    4. Archery
    5. Spearwall: Kopeyshchik and Hanse Stadt Miliz hit enemy horse
    6. Horse melee
    7. Foot melee

    Gameplay mod · 2024

    Bitter Heretic

    A melee mod for Heretic, played on GZDoom. Punching-focused combat: weaker ranged attacks, harder melee, slower and better-telegraphed monsters, blocking that stuns, shields that deflect projectiles, and pushbacks. Low magic.

    Download Bitter_Heretic.pk3 (96 MB) → · ZDoom forum thread

    • GZDoom
    • One .pk3 file
    • New monster sprites in 2025

    What it changes

    • 15 weapons, each with an alt fire and a reload. Three grenades on quick keys. No running.
    • New death, wound, melee and pain animations for every monster; smooth 12-frame walks for the golem, gargoyle, knight, sabreclaw and wendigo (10 for the weredragon).
    • Blocking stuns a monster that hits you in melee; shields deflect projectiles.
    • Tweaked pickups and artifacts with quick-use keys, and Neural hi-res textures (monsters excluded).
    • Door keys are randomised: 3 of 6 colours each map. Pistol start by default.
    • Includes the PY weapon wheel (Caps Lock) and a Fullscreen Status Bar, plus dynamic lights on weapons and decorations for DarkDoom.
    • Caps Lockweapon wheel
    • Rreload

    How to play it

    1. Load the .pk3 files with ZDL.
    2. Add a dark lighting mod such as Dark Doom Z.
    3. For endless maps, generate them with Obsidian and its Heathen's Maze addon.
    4. Or play hand-made maps: Sold Soul, Quest for the Crystal Skull, The Wayfarer.

    New monsters and fixes

    The Broken Coast against an AI

    The Broken Coast scenario redrawn as a plain hex grid with lettered columns and numbered rows. With coordinates like E13 or G12, an AI chat can follow the board, play the other side and suggest moves, recruits and attacks.

    The Wrath of the Crooked Beak

    A two-player (or solo, two-handed) variant with no scenarios and no seasons. Read the rules on BoardGameGeek →

    Objectives

    Each player picks two Settlements as the opponent's Objectives. You win the moment your units stand on both of yours at once. Placing them is a little game of its own.

    Fatigue and Exhaustion

    A unit that acts or is attacked is Fatigued; a second attack Exhausts it. A surviving Exhausted defender must fall back, and the attacker must advance.

    Retreat

    A faster or Flying target may decline combat before any dice or spells, but it ends Fatigued, so pinning it down just takes more attacks.

    Economy

    10 gold of opening Armies and one random Hero. Income is 3 plus 1 per Settlement; destroyed Armies are gone for good.

    Remake · 2026 · playable

    Aethra Chronicles

    A playable browser remake of The Aethra Chronicles, Vol. 1: Celystra's Bane (1994), built from the original game files so the art can be redrawn piece by piece.

    • 40 maps: 1 world, 16 towns, 23 dungeon levels
    • HTML + JavaScript, no build step
    • Runs from one HTML file

    What works

    • Every map, with the links between them: the world, 16 towns and 23 dungeon levels.
    • Shops with the original stock and prices, inns, guild training, temples and hired mercenaries.
    • Locked doors, traps, hidden passages, and chests with the original loot. Dungeons are dark until you light a torch.
    • Tactical combat on the map around the party. Characters walk with their movement points and attack by walking into an enemy; bows and spells need a clear line of sight.
    • Saving and loading, with quest progress kept in the save.
    • WASDmove
    • Ccast
    • Fsearch for hidden doors
    • Tlight a torch
    • Rcamp

    The story is data

    Each story event in quests.json lists conditions on quest flags, then actions: show text, give or take items and gold, start a fight, add a companion. All dialogue is read from the original game's text file, and its numbered choices become buttons. The rules and rewards follow the original game code.

    • The Old Vizier
    • Merchant Harmon's painting
    • The red dragon
    • The Oracle's four Power Gems
    • The King Sword
    • The Ring Mountain
    • The demon Toneath
    • The bounty on Galoran
    • Father Gyman

    Made to be redrawn

    Every picture is a sprite sheet on a fixed grid. Repaint a sheet at 2× or 4× the size and the game picks it up and draws it at the original size. One command packs the game, its art and its data into a single HTML file that runs by double-clicking it in Chrome, Edge or Firefox.

    Cyclades variant

    House rules for Cyclades, tried out at the table: a three-player setup, a cadet variant, reworked god boards for Apollo and Athena, and new texts for heroes and creatures.

    Kakó Máti rules on BoardGameGeek →

    • 3-player variant
    • Cadet variant

    Kakó Máti rules

    Setup and combat

    With 2 or 3 players, double the bidding tokens; the Priestess discount applies to one only. Everyone starts with 10 coins. Dice are multiplied by force.

    Buildings

    A Fortress soaks the first hit. A Port allows Sea Moves for 1 gold from its sea, a University Land Moves for 1 gold (with attack) from its land. Not for Ares or Apollo.

    Gods

    Apollo swaps 1 Philosopher for a displayed hero and places 2 Cornucopias on two different seas. Athena can also build up to 3 Fleets for 2 gold each.

    Monsters

    Hydra makes every faction lose a troop or fleet in or next to its area, with no income bonus. Pegasus moves one hero. Charon swaps a Philosopher for a random hero. The Cyclops can swap opponents' buildings too.

    Heroes such as Helen (her die is always 1), Croesus and Jason get new texts, and a Metropolis from a sacrifice costs an extra Philosopher. Everything fits on one A4 sheet to glue onto the components.

    Heroes

    New card texts

    • Hydra: each faction destroys one of its own Fleets or Troops in the Hydra's area or next to it.
    • A hero who can use his own Fleets as Troops when making a Heroic Move.
    • Place 2 Cornucopias in 2 different areas that have none yet.
    • Move one of your heroes from one land area to another.

    Board game variant · 2026

    Yulin: South China Sea

    A streamlined ruleset for South China Sea: Modern Naval Conflict that plays more like a game than a wargame. Fewer rules to track, more decisions that matter.

    Download all files to print →

    • One d6 per strike
    • 66 custom 15 mm counters
    • New Chinese unit: maritime militia

    What changes

    Fast dice

    One d6 per strike, weapon scores from 0 to 3. A natural 1 or 2 always misses, so most rolls need no maths. Full-strength counters strike twice, reduced ones once and gain +1 Stealth.

    Ammo

    Rolling a 1 and a 6 marks a ship Low Ammo; its next shot leaves it with No Ammo.

    Air defence

    Ships and ground batteries have an AA score and can hit aircraft in range of the Focus hex. A Spent air-defence unit only protects itself, opening gaps to strike carriers.

    Engagement

    Five steps: AA, AS, U, AG, G. Strike order follows Stealth only; on a tie the attacker starts and sides alternate one counter at a time. Targets in littoral hexes are 1 harder to hit.

    Evade

    Moving into enemy weapon range, you declare Evade. If it works, the group moves before combat and can't strike or be struck; if it fails, it moves after combat.

    Illumination

    Ships 5, AA ground batteries 2, submarines, militia and ground units 1, aircraft 0.

    Maritime militia: a Chinese fishing fleet that slows US movement, provides illumination, makes evading harder and soaks up US missiles.

    Board game variant · 2025

    Eclipse: Second Dawn variant

    House rules for Eclipse: Second Dawn for the Galaxy that skip the long economic build-up. Set up in three rounds at most, then keep throwing punches.

    Read the rules on BoardGameGeek →

    • Double starting resources
    • Research + Upgrade in one action
    • Monoliths from turn one

    Quicker start

    • Double starting Materials, Science and Money. Each player starts with 3 Interceptors and 1 Cruiser (Orion: 2 Cruisers).
    • Take four starting sectors (I, II, III, III) around your home, with their discovery tiles. They count toward the sector III limit.
    • Discovery tiles are drawn from the black bag when revealed or when Ancients are cleared; reputation tiles are not used.

    What changes

    Actions

    Research and Upgrade are one action. Discoveries must be used (no 2 VP option) and explored sectors must be placed. No diplomats or traitors.

    Specialised population

    At round end, spend 3 Colony Ships to place a Diplomat on your mat with a population cube of your choice on top (+1 VP). Up to 3.

    Combat

    Cannons hit on 5+, missiles on 6. No reputation draws. Dreadnoughts carry up to 4 Interceptors. Lost ships give Science: Interceptor 1, Cruiser 3, Dreadnought 4, Starbase 2.

    Monoliths

    Buildable from the start for 10 Materials, each worth 1 VP per round. Ships with 3 spare power can jump between Monoliths and warp portals.

    Tech tweaks

    Neutron bombs strike before combat. Gauss and Phase Shields protect planets. Improved Hull costs 1 initiative. Ancient Lab grants an extra Research action.

    Factions

    Planta specialises with 2 Colony Ships but loses its per-sector VP. Mechanema starts with one fewer Colony Ship.

    Being tested: spend 10 Science on a discovery tile instead of a technology.

    Board game variant · 2024

    Trolls and Princesses variant

    Deflation, swift trolls and even more dismayed princesses. House rules that cut downtime, rebalance scoring away from item sets and make kidnapping princesses actually happen.

    Read the rules on BoardGameGeek →

    • One troll move per turn
    • Item sets 1/3/5 VP
    • Always 4 villages

    What changes

    Swift trolls

    One troll move per turn instead of two. Trolls outside Cauldrons wait in supply; two can go to one place only if at least one comes from supply.

    Deflation

    Item sets score 1/3/5 instead of 4/9/15, a princess 6 VP, so blue caves and Troll Cards matter.

    Princesses

    Capturing one takes 4 trolls and brings a troll changeling to your board instead of a King tile, unlocking an upgrade.

    Private King goals

    Each player gets three hidden King Cards, one per colour. King tiles are drawn at random, so no one builds around the broken ones.

    Villages

    Always four villages with one Human each. All Round Cards form one shared stack; draw 2, not 3. Hiring a Human costs no energy, a changeling 1.

    Caves

    New cave tiles get resources on their mining symbols. The replenish action mines 1 Obsidian instead. Displays refill only by action.

    Smaller tweaks: the changeling barn spot gives a whole barn, and Red starts with 1 Obsidian.

    At the table

    A three-player game took two hours, scored 48, 45 and 35. Players new to the game praised how smoothly it ran.

    Board game variant · 2019–2020

    Polished Risk: LotR

    Reworked rules and Adventure Cards for Risk: The Lord of the Rings. Balanced units, all-in battles and a reason to hold land, so doom stacks take time and losing players can recover.

    Download the rules →

    • d6, d8 and d10 dice
    • Custom Adventure Cards
    • Homemade player banners

    What changes

    Units

    Cavalry costs 2, rolls a d6, adds +1 to any die and moves two territories. A Monster costs 3 and removes one enemy unit outright, no roll.

    Battles

    Attacker and defender roll with all their units at once instead of 3 dice against 2.

    Production

    A new phase: if you don't move your army, draw territory cards equal to the lands you control divided by 3.

    Setup

    At most 4 units per territory at the start. No Ring movement, which slowed round counting without affecting the game.

    Adventure Cards

    • No man can kill me: on another player's turn, they make only half their attack rolls (rounded up).
    • It is not this day: defending on that player's turn, you hit on 2+.
    • Cave Troll and Entmoot: remove half the units (rounded up) from the target territory, a nuke for doom stacks.

    You'll need a banner per player (a button, a toothpick and a sticky note), an extra sea lane drawn on the board, and sleeves for the custom cards.

    Original board game · area control

    Delusional Invasion

    An area control game where disasters decide the winner. Each Disaster that strikes goes to whoever has the most buildings and ships, and the most Disasters at the end wins.

    • 3 actions a turn
    • Cities, Wilds, Points of Interest, Seas
    • One deck: disasters and benefits

    How it plays

    Turns

    Take three actions: Build, Build ship, Recruit, March, Sail, Reposition, Exploit or Uprising, each at most once, or play cards from hand as often as you like.

    Exploit and disasters

    Draw a card per Point of Interest you control. Every Disaster drawn (Winter, Fire, Disease, Flood, Famine, Storm, Brood, Levy) hits all players at once.

    Units

    Core units fight at 1, Elites at 2 and capture buildings and ships instead of destroying them. Monsters, summoned in the Wilds, fight at 0 but kill a unit.

    Combat

    Each side may play one card. Add strength; the defender wins ties. The winner scatters the loser's army into its adjacent zones, then monsters and kill cards take casualties.

    Buildings and ships

    Buildings hold zones without troops and let armies Reposition along a chain of built-up zones. Ships carry armies by sea and add strength in naval battles.

    Terrain

    Rivers and mountains block movement. Road, Boats and Flight cards get around them.

    Wargame rules · 2023–2026

    Age of Fantasy: Battalion

    Rank-and-file fantasy battles on multibased units. Alternating activations, simultaneous melee, and one golden rule: roll the dice right now, check stats and cover after.

    Download the rules (PDF, 0.7 MB) →

    • 4 rounds
    • “1 me – 1 you” activation
    • Damage marked with dice

    How it plays

    Orders

    Each activation gives a unit one order: Hold, Advance (6″), Rush (12″, no shooting) or Charge (12″). A random side starts each of the four rounds.

    Attacks

    Roll Attack dice against the target's Defense; a 6 always wounds, a 1 always fails. Tough is how many wounds a unit takes before it's removed. Damage never reduces attacks.

    Fatigue and Evasion

    A unit that has attacked is Fatigued, and its enemies gain Evasion, a second save. Cover, hindered charges and flanks add Evasion too.

    Melee and morale

    Charged units fight each other at once and stay locked in. Wounds plus Combat Resolution decide the loser, who tests Morale on 4+ or flees to the table edge.

    Spells

    Spells always succeed, ignore cover and reach 18″. A wizard can't repeat a spell until the others have been cast.

    Gear and rules

    Spears give Phalanx, lances Impact, paired weapons Rage, great weapons AP. Leadership lets a commander activate nearby units together.

    Orders

    Tabletop RPG rules · 2014 · Polish

    Cep Wojenny

    A reworked mechanic for the second edition of Warhammer Fantasy Roleplay: fewer, clearer attributes, no secondary stats, and creature size that actually matters.

    • 46 pages
    • k100 tests
    • Basic and advanced careers

    What changes

    Eight attributes

    Weapon Skill, Ballistic Skill, Build, Agility, Reason, Will, Fellowship and Perception. Strength and Toughness merge into Build; Perception splits off from Intelligence. Secondary stats are gone.

    Size

    Creatures fall into size classes from very small to very large, each shifting damage dice, so a horse with low Build still outmuscles a strong dog.

    No Fate, no Fortune

    Spend 3 XP to escape death, and the GM may send a mundane misfortune in return. Spend a Vitality token to reroll, take an extra action or make an extra attack.

    Players roll

    Only players make tests: the GM reveals an NPC's stats and a player rolls for the opposed test. Rerolls come as rerolls of failure and of success.

    Board game redesign · Polish

    Srebrna Flota

    “Olej kokosowy” (Coconut Oil), a 2018 redesign inspired by Srebrna Flota, the 1994 No1 Novina game. One player sails Spain's silver fleet across the map to the open sea; the other leads corsairs trying to steal as much silver as they can.

    Download on BoardGameGeek →

    • 2+ players
    • 8 ship types, 40 ships
    • Polish, print and play

    What's in it

    Ships

    Carrack, galleon, pinnace, caravel, fluyt, frigate, brigantine and sloop, each rated for hull, speed, turning, heavy, medium and light guns, crew and cargo. Barrel-hulled Spanish ships are tough and roomy; long-hulled corsair ships are fast and cheap.

    Silver

    Spain earns silver for every ton delivered; corsairs earn far more for each ton they sell. Crew takes up cargo space, and a full broadside needs enough sailors.

    Wind and turns

    Each turn starts with a wind roll that can shift its direction and strength, then the sides alternate activating ships.

    Components

    Rules, a starting sheet, two-sided sails and bases for 40 hull miniatures (or cardboard), ship logs, and a 50×60 cm hex map.
